newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Kia ends price discounts on cars.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Kia ends price discounts on cars.

text.p: South Korea's struggling Kia Group ended deep price discounts on its main car models late on Tuesday because of depleted inventories, a group spokesman said on Wednesday.
Kia Motor Sales Co, the sales affiliate of the eighth largest industrial group, on Sunday began selling passenger and commercial vehicles at a 29.9 percent cash discount to raise money.
"We had to end the discount programme on passenger cars because we are almost out of inventories," the spokesman said.
Sales of Kia's cars surged after Kia announced the discount offer. The spokesman said Kia had sold nearly 50,000 vehicles in the past three days. Most were cars, he said.
Kia's previous daily sales averaged 900 to 1,000 passenger and commercial vehicles, he said.
Kia will continue to offer a discount on commercial vehicles until the end of this month.
The deep price cut, aimed at raising cash for the troubled group, applied only to cash payments.
The discounted models were Sephia and Avella compact cars, Credos mid-sized sedans and Sportage utility vehicles.
Asia Motors, commercial vehicle unit of Kia Group, also began selling its products at discount from Monday until the end of this month.
Asia Motors is offering 20-29.9 percent discounts for large trucks and 20 percent for mini-trucks. For buses, 15-27 percent discounts will be offered.
Creditor banks decided last week to rescue the Kia Group, whose carmaking unit was battered by slumping domestic sales.
